info.effectsHeading: What changes when you edit it

platform_fee_percentage.controls: The percentage of the sale amount SellWell takes on every confirmed sale. Stored on every new lead at submission time as `platform_fee_amount`, then released to SellWell from the company's escrow when the sale is confirmed.
platform_fee_percentage.effects: Lowering this reduces what SellWell earns per sale. Raising it increases the company's total cost (commission + fee). Existing leads keep their stamped fee — only NEW leads submitted after the change use the new percentage.

escrow_min_deposit_da.controls: The smallest amount (in DA) a Tech Company can deposit into its escrow wallet in a single top-up. Enforced both on /escrow/fund (page validator) and in `fundWallet` (server defense-in-depth).
escrow_min_deposit_da.effects: Lowering this lets companies fund tiny amounts (useful for testing). Raising it blocks companies from topping up below the new floor on their next /escrow/fund visit — existing deposits are untouched.

lead_acknowledgment_window_days.controls: The number of days a Tech Company has after a partner submits a lead to reserve escrow & reveal the client's contact info. After this, the lead is considered expired and the partner is free to re-submit it elsewhere.
lead_acknowledgment_window_days.effects: Lowering this shortens the company's window — partners get their leads back to use elsewhere faster. Raising it gives companies more breathing room but delays the partner. Affects the derived `ack_deadline` on every submitted lead immediately.

client_verification_timeout_days.controls: The number of days SellWell waits for a client to reply during a dispute (when admin contacts the client to verify a sale) before escalating to admin investigation.
client_verification_timeout_days.effects: Lowering this means disputes escalate to manual admin review sooner — more admin work, faster resolution. Raising it gives clients longer to reply on their own. Affects the derived `verification_deadline` on every dispute row immediately.

reapplication_cooldown_days.controls: The number of days a rejected Sales Partner must wait before they can re-apply to join the platform. Enforced both in the user-facing /settings banner countdown AND in the server-side `resubmitForReview` guard.
reapplication_cooldown_days.effects: Lowering this lets rejected partners re-apply sooner. Raising it adds friction. Partners currently inside the cooldown will see the remaining countdown shift the next time the page renders.

partner_link_attribution_window_days.controls: The number of days a Partner Link click remains eligible for attribution. If the client converts within this window via the link, the partner gets the commission. Last-click wins.
partner_link_attribution_window_days.effects: Lowering this tightens attribution — only fresh clicks count. Raising it gives partners credit for longer-lead-time sales. Affects every new click recorded after the change; old clicks keep their original expiry.

click_dedup_window_minutes.controls: The number of minutes during which the same IP + same Partner Link doesn't double-count as a new click. Prevents refresh-spamming a link to inflate the counter.
click_dedup_window_minutes.effects: Lowering this is more permissive (each click counts faster). Raising it is stricter (a visitor's repeated clicks in this window count as one). Affects new clicks recorded after the change.

max_upload_size_mb.controls: The largest single file (in MB) any FileInput on the platform accepts by default. Some specific inputs override this with a tighter cap (e.g. 5 MB for image thumbnails) — those stay tighter regardless of this setting.
max_upload_size_mb.effects: Lowering this rejects bigger uploads platform-wide. Raising it loosens the limit. Affects every NEW upload attempt after the change — already-uploaded files aren't re-validated.

FAQ.headline: Questions you might have
FAQ.subtitle: Two sides, same answers — pick yours.
FAQ.company1Q: What does it cost to list a product?
FAQ.company1A: Nothing. Listing is free. Approving partners is free. You only pay when you confirm a sale — when a partner has closed a real deal and you've sold your product. The 10% platform fee and the partner's commission release from your escrow only at that confirmation. No subscription, no setup fee, no monthly cost.
FAQ.company2Q: How does the escrow wallet actually work?
FAQ.company2A: The wallet is your money sitting on the platform. You fund it any amount you want via Chargily Pay. When a partner submits a hot lead, you reserve commission + platform fee from that wallet to view the contact details. If the deal closes you confirm and the reservation pays out. If it doesn't, the reservation returns — your wallet, untouched.
FAQ.company3Q: Can I get my escrow money back?
FAQ.company3A: Yes, any time. Your available balance — anything not currently reserved against a live lead — can be withdrawn back to the original payment method. Or you can keep it and use it on the next lead. It's your money on your terms.
FAQ.company4Q: What stops a partner from claiming a deal my own team already closed?
FAQ.company4A: Two things. First, duplicate detection: the same client phone or email submitted to the same campaign is rejected — first submission wins. Second, the tracking window: a lead is locked to the partner who registered it for 30, 60, or 90 days (you choose). After that it's released.
FAQ.company5Q: What if a partner brings me a fake or unqualified lead?
FAQ.company5A: You report it. SellWell contacts the client to verify. Partners with repeated fake-lead reports are flagged and eventually suspended. Every partner applies per-campaign with a written pitch — you approve who represents your product.
FAQ.partner1Q: Is this just affiliate marketing in disguise?
FAQ.partner1A: No. This is a platform for professional B2B salespeople — people who pitch, qualify, and close. Every partner applies to a campaign with a written pitch. Companies approve who sells their product. No bloggers, no influencers, no signup-and-spam links.
FAQ.partner2A: The day the deal closes. For offline leads, the company confirms the sale on the platform and your commission releases from their escrow to your earnings the same day. For Partner Link sales, payment splits at checkout via Chargily Pay — you're credited automatically.
FAQ.partner3Q: Is the commission really 100%, or are there hidden deductions?
FAQ.partner3A: 100%. The platform fee is paid by the company on top of the commission, not deducted from it. If a campaign offers 10,000 DA commission, you receive exactly 10,000 DA.
FAQ.partner4Q: What if a company denies a sale I actually closed?
FAQ.partner4A: SellWell contacts the client directly to verify. If the client confirms the sale, the company's escrow releases your commission and the company is flagged. Three flags trigger an investigation. The verification flow protects you.
FAQ.partner5Q: Can I sell on multiple campaigns at the same time?
FAQ.partner5A: Yes. Apply to as many campaigns as fit your skills. You build one professional profile (channels, experience, prior conversion record) and use it across every application.
FAQ.links1A: A tracked URL approved partners can share. SellWell records the click then redirects instantly to the merchant's own product or pricing page — the client barely registers passing through. When the client buys on the merchant's site, the sale is auto-attributed to the partner via a Chargily webhook. Used for online-payable products like SaaS subscriptions where the deal can close in a self-serve checkout.
FAQ.links2Q: When should I use a Partner Link instead of registering a hot lead?
FAQ.links2A: Use Partner Links when the company offers them and the product can be bought online (typical for SaaS subscriptions, training, digital products). Use lead registration for high-touch B2B deals that close offline — most enterprise software, anything over a few hundred thousand DA.
FAQ.links3Q: How is a Partner Link sale paid?
FAQ.links3A: The client pays the merchant directly via Chargily Pay on the merchant's own site — SellWell never holds the customer's payment. When Chargily's webhook tells SellWell the payment succeeded, the partner's commission and the platform fee are recorded against the sale; commission accrues to the partner's withdrawable balance and the platform fee is invoiced to the merchant. No escrow involved.
FAQ.links4Q: How does attribution work — what if the client buys later?
FAQ.links4A: Each click is logged with a timestamp and a hashed IP. The same client clicking your link and buying within the dedup window counts as one click. Attribution sticks to the partner who shared the link the client used.
FAQ.links5Q: Can a company turn off Partner Links for their campaign?
FAQ.links5A: Yes. Each campaign has a Partner Links toggle. Some companies prefer offline-only because their product doesn't sell self-serve. The campaign's listing tells you upfront which flow is allowed.
FAQ.pricing1A: A platform fee of 10% on the sale amount, paid only when three things have all happened: the deal closes, you've actually received the client's payment, and you confirm the sale on SellWell. Nothing leaves your escrow before that. No subscription, no listing fee, no signup cost, no monthly minimum — every dinar in your wallet stays yours until you confirm a real, paid deal.
FAQ.pricing2Q: Is the fee 10% of the commission or 10% of the sale?
FAQ.pricing2A: 10% of the sale amount. If a product sells for 100,000 DA at a 10% commission rate, the partner earns 10,000 DA, the company pays a 10,000 DA platform fee, and the company's total cost on that deal is 20,000 DA. The partner keeps the full 10,000.
FAQ.pricing3Q: When is the platform fee charged?
FAQ.pricing3A: Only when a deal is confirmed. For offline leads, when the company confirms the sale. For Partner Link sales, automatically at checkout. If a deal doesn't close, the company pays nothing.
FAQ.pricing4A: No. Listing is free. Joining is free. Funding the escrow uses standard Chargily Pay processing rates (set by Chargily, not SellWell). Withdrawing escrow back is free. Partner payouts are free.
FAQ.pricing5A: The fee is a platform setting and may be adjusted in the future, but any change applies only to deals after the change. Existing campaigns and in-progress reservations honor the fee at the time the lead was submitted.

Problem.headline: Selling software in Algeria is harder than building it
Problem.card1Body: Building an in-house team takes months, costs salaries and benefits, and doesn't guarantee results.
Problem.card2Body: Ads bring clicks, not clients. In Algeria, B2B sales happen through trust and real conversations.
Problem.card3Body: Spreadsheets, missed commissions, payment disputes. Without a platform, it doesn't scale.
Problem.closing: There's a better way to sell software in Algeria.

close.body: The campaign is no longer accepting leads or applications.

pause.title: Pause this campaign?
pause.description: Partners will see a Paused badge on the listing. They can't submit new leads while paused. You can resume any time.

resume.title: Resume this campaign?
resume.description: The listing returns to Active. Partners can submit leads as soon as you confirm.

close.title: Close this campaign?
close.description: Closing is permanent. The campaign disappears from the marketplace and partners can't submit new leads. Historical data is preserved.

edit.toastErrorBody: Something went wrong. Try again in a moment.

overview.productImageHelper: JPG, PNG, or WEBP. Up to 5 MB. Shown as the listing thumbnail.
overview.productTagsHelper: Pick one or more tags so partners can filter to your product.
overview.targetIndustriesHelper: Industries this product is built for. Helps partners find the right buyers.
overview.requirementsHelper: Optional. Explain experience or context partners need to sell this well.

pricing.helper: Add one tier for fixed-price products, or several to expose Starter / Pro / Enterprise. The commission is calculated per tier.

commission.valueHelperPct: Whole or decimal value, e.g. 10 for 10%.
commission.trackingWindowHelper: How long an offline lead stays locked to the partner who submitted it.

salesKit.intro: Optional sales-enablement materials your partners use to pitch the product. Skip any slot that doesn't apply.
salesKit.slotPitchDeckHelper: PDF, PPTX, JPG, or PNG. Up to 25 MB.
salesKit.slotOnePagerHelper: PDF, JPG, or PNG. Up to 25 MB.
salesKit.slotPricingSheetHelper: PDF, PPTX, or XLSX. Up to 25 MB.
salesKit.videoUrlError: Use a YouTube, Loom, or Vimeo URL.
salesKit.fileHelper: Drag a file here or click to browse.
salesKit.otherLabelPlaceholder: Label (e.g. Customer case study — Atlas SARL)
salesKit.unpreviewableBody: This file type can't be previewed inline. Download to open it.

partnerLinks.toggleHelper: Lets partners share a tracked URL for online sales. SellWell records the click and attributes the sale via your Chargily webhook.
partnerLinks.redirectUrlHelper: Where sellwell.dz/r/[code] 302s to. Usually your product or pricing page.
partnerLinks.secretHelper: Copy from your Chargily dashboard. Used to verify incoming webhook signatures.
partnerLinks.testHelper: Sends a synthetic checkout.paid to your endpoint to confirm the secret works.
partnerLinks.testSuccessBody: Your endpoint accepted the synthetic event.
partnerLinks.testErrorBody: Double-check the URL and secret, then try again.

adminForward.title: This is the company campaign-management view.
adminForward.body: Admins manage campaigns from the admin panel. The admin-facing campaign view ships in Phase 9 (Admin).

wizard.title: Create campaign
wizard.description: List your product with commission terms so sales partners can apply and start sending you leads.

publishGate.pendingReview: Your account is pending admin approval. Save as draft until approved.
publishGate.webhookRequired: Test your webhook before publishing with Partner Links enabled.

toast.draftSaved: Your campaign has been saved as a draft.
toast.saveError: Couldn't save the draft. Try again.
toast.published: Your campaign is now live on the marketplace.
toast.publishError: Couldn't publish the campaign. Try again.

step1.descriptionPlaceholder: Describe your product, what it does, and who it's for…
step1.productImageHelper: JPG or PNG, max 5 MB. Shown on the marketplace card.
step1.productTagsHelper: Select up to 5 tags that describe your product.
step1.requirementsPlaceholder: What experience or profile should applicants have?…

step2.tiersHelper: Add at least one tier. For a single fixed price, add one tier — the tier name is optional and will display as "Standard" if left blank.
step2.singleTierTip: Most campaigns have a single fixed price. Add more tiers only if your product genuinely has a Starter / Pro / Enterprise split with different price points.
step2.fixedPriceHelper: The price a client pays. Partners see this when submitting a lead.
step2.addTierInfo: Add a pricing tier if your product has different plans (e.g. Starter, Pro, Enterprise) with distinct prices. Each tier will be selectable by Sales Partners when submitting a lead.

step3.commissionPctHelper: e.g. 10 means the partner earns 10% of each closed deal.
step3.commissionFlatHelper: Partners earn this fixed amount per confirmed sale, regardless of tier price.
step3.trackingWindowHelper: Time during which a registered lead is locked to the Sales Partner. After this window, if no sale is confirmed, the lead may expire.
step3.partnerLinksLabel: Enable Partner Links for this campaign
step3.partnerLinksHelper: Sales partners generate a tracked URL (sellwell.dz/r/…) that 302-redirects to your product page. SellWell never holds the payment — your Chargily checkout is the merchant of record.
step3.merchantRedirectHelper: The page Sales Partners will send traffic to. Your Chargily checkout should be reachable from this page.
step3.webhookSecretPlaceholder: Paste your Chargily webhook signing secret…
step3.webhookSecretHelper: From your Chargily dashboard → Webhooks → copy the signing secret for the sellwell.dz/api/webhooks/chargily endpoint.
step3.snippetCapture: 1 — Capture sw_click on your landing page
step3.snippetCheckout: 2 — Pass sw_click through your Chargily checkout
step3.testWebhookHelper: Fire a synthetic checkout.paid event to verify your webhook secret is correctly configured. Required before you can publish.
step3.testWebhookPassed: Webhook test passed — your secret is correctly configured.
step3.testWebhookSuccess: Your webhook secret is correct. You can now publish with Partner Links enabled.
step3.testWebhookError: Couldn't verify your webhook. Double-check the secret and try again.

step4.intro: All slots are optional. Upload materials that help your Sales Partners pitch your product more effectively.
step4.slotPitchDeckHelper: Used by partners on first calls. PDF or PPTX.
step4.slotOnePagerHelper: Single page — what / who / why. PDF or image.
step4.slotPricingSheetHelper: Detailed price grid for negotiations. PDF, PPTX or XLSX.
step4.slotDemoVideoHelper: YouTube, Loom or Vimeo link. Shown as a watchable embed.
step4.videoUrlError: Please enter a valid YouTube, Loom or Vimeo URL.
step4.fileHelper: PDF, PPTX, JPG, PNG or ZIP — max 25 MB.
step4.unpreviewableBody: Download the file to view it.

step5.intro: Review your campaign before publishing. Missing required fields are highlighted below.
step5.webhookTestRequired: You must pass the webhook test before publishing with Partner Links enabled.
